# `git merge --squash` fires post-merge even when it conflicted, with the
# conflicts still sitting in the index. Revealing there would overwrite the
# driver's merge result with our side, so the hook keeps its hands off.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

cp base.txt $TMPDIR/base.txt
cp ours.txt $TMPDIR/ours.txt
cp theirs.txt $TMPDIR/theirs.txt

exec sesam init --user admin --install-merge
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

cp $TMPDIR/base.txt s
exec sesam add s --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add secret'

exec git checkout -b topic
cp $TMPDIR/theirs.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'topic: change s'

exec git checkout master
cp $TMPDIR/ours.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'master: change s'

! exec git merge --squash topic

# The markers the driver wrote survive the hook.
grep '^<<<<<<< ' s
grep 'OURS' s
grep 'THEIRS' s

# A squash sets no MERGE_HEAD, so it used to look like "no merge at all" and skip
# the finalize. SQUASH_MSG gives it away instead.
exec sesam status
stdout 'conflicted'
stdout 'a squash merge is in progress'
stdout 'git commit'
! stdout 'abort'

# The finalize therefore refuses the markers, as it would in a plain merge.
exec git add -A
! exec git commit -m squashed
stderr 'unresolved conflicts in this squash merge'

# Resolving lets it through, and the squashed commit is consistent.
cp $TMPDIR/ours.txt s
exec git commit -m squashed
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/s.sesam
stdout 'OURS'
exec sesam verify
stderr 'Integrity: ok'
exec sesam status
! stdout 'in progress'

-- base.txt --
line one
BASE
line three
-- ours.txt --
line one
OURS
line three
-- theirs.txt --
line one
THEIRS
line three
